answer: Sybil resistance is a lee-slope imprint gate. An applicant books one numbered stake on a charted dune and is issued a one-shot zinc stencil whose cut-out text is a registrar-chosen fable. Only that operator may bed the stencil at the official marker; after a measured watch a ranger, navigating solely by a sealed atlas leaf for that slope, lifts it and compares the wind-etched imprint to the original cuts. Minting many identities requires leasing many exclusive stakes and staying on site for the unannounced lift, because a moved or reused stencil leaves a doubled scar the photograph rejects.
